clue.text: Cheerless changing of sides during half-time?

indicators.note: sides are right and left, so within the interval word one side letter is swapped for the other

blocks.note: the break between the two halves of a match

explanation.surface: A football team trudges through a dismal half-time as the players swap ends.
explanation.walkthrough: In BREAK the R (right) is changed to L (left), just as teams change sides at the interval.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak describes a dreary, comfortless outlook or mood, a close synonym of joyless and gloomy.

clue.text: Tradesman’s exorbitant amount is wasted — zero’s banked

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined and broken up, so the following letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper overcharges wildly, and the money paid in has vanished to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A BAKER'S DOZEN is thirteen, one more than the expected twelve, so it is the tradesman's generous over-the-top amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers traditionally gave thirteen loaves when twelve were ordered, an extra measure beyond the usual count.

clue.text: I lift skinned rabbit

indicators.note: skinning strips off the outside, so the first and last letters are removed
in a down clue lifting raises the letters so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Roger Rabbit, the cartoon star of Who Framed Roger Rabbit

explanation.surface: A cook hoists a freshly skinned rabbit off the table.
explanation.walkthrough: ROGER loses its outer letters to leave OGE, which is read upwards as EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is the Latin first-person pronoun and the psychological term for one's sense of self.

clue.text: Deathwatch taking place after cat caught bird

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so the cat word is taken by its sound
says the vigil word is placed after the cat word in the answer

blocks.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat, spelt here to match the bird
a wake is a watch kept over a dead body

explanation.surface: A deathwatch beetle is caught by a cat that has just taken a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of northern seas, named for its call.

clue.text: Old entry in early bird’s journal?

blocks.note: first meaning: decrepit, riddled with holes, antiquated
second meaning: the early bird catches its prey, so its diary records what it had for breakfast

explanation.surface: An old diary entry written by someone who rises at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the early bird catches the worm, so a bird's diary entry would record the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood or furniture bored through by grubs looks ancient and decayed, so the phrase also means antiquated.

clue.text: Go with male model on day/days off

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it, so the male model precedes the day

blocks.note: to go is a childish word for urinate, as is wee
Ken is Barbie's boyfriend doll
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A timetable note for a fashion model about which days he is free.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday and Sunday are the usual rest days from work, the two-day break each week.

clue.text: Wine in unopened box tipped over

indicators.note: without its opening, the container word loses its first letter
something tipped over is upended, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a canister is a small box or tin

explanation.surface: Wine stored in a box that someone knocked over before it was opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Especially old carriage quietly departs

indicators.note: the quiet letter leaves, so it is taken out of the carriage word

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
p is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: An especially old coach slips quietly away from the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra used as an adverb means unusually or particularly, as in extra careful.

clue.text: Sweet song from the fifties

blocks.note: first meaning: a confection or ice cream of mixed chopped fruits
second meaning: Little Richard's 1955 rock and roll hit

explanation.surface: A fond memory of a lovely tune from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase for all fruits names both a candied-fruit dessert and a famous early rock record.

clue.text: News article bores old lady

indicators.note: boring drills into something, so the article goes inside

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new, so news is read as two of them
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece so dull that it puts an elderly woman to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan is an informal word for grandmother, an elderly female relative.

clue.text: Wild kittens love time inside? Most puzzling…

indicators.note: wild animals run riot, so the young cats' letters are scrambled
says the love and time letters go within the jumbled word

blocks.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Untamed kittens adore staying indoors, which is a real mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is intricate and hard to solve, so the superlative is the hardest to work out.

clue.text: Giant bird with many wings taking flight

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters, and they fly away

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge bird with many wings takes to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the gigantic gods of Greek myth, so the name now means any colossus.

clue.text: Turning a letter in Scrabble to make SNAKE?

definitions.note: a snake is one kind, hence the question mark

indicators.note: turning something round makes its letters run backwards

blocks.note: per means a, as in once a day or per day
each Scrabble letter is printed on a small tile

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player flips over one tile to complete the word SNAKE.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAKE in capitals looks like a word on the Scrabble board, but it is just the definition, made more general by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes are cold-blooded scaly vertebrates, one example of the class that includes lizards and crocodiles.

clue.text: Say, Rachmaninov, Brahms and Liszt only appear around one

indicators.note: Brahms and Liszt is rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk, so the letters reel about
the phrase goes round the single letter before everything is mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Three great Romantic composers only make an appearance around one o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Brahms and Liszt look like more composers alongside Rachmaninov, but together they are British rhyming slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachmaninov was a celebrated virtuoso pianist as well as a composer, an example of a keyboard performer.

clue.text: Characters leaning forward, one covered in talc, one beginning to sling bottles

indicators.note: one covered in powder has the powder all round it
the beginning of a word is its first letter
to bottle is to hold inside, so the second one and the initial enclose the powdered piece

blocks.note: Roman numeral one, the second one in the clue
taken as written
Roman numeral one, the first one in the clue
first letter of sling

explanation.surface: A baby dusted with talc sits beside another who is about to throw bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two ones: the first sits in the talc, and the second, with the S, does the bottling round the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slopes to the right, so its printed letters appear to lean ahead.

clue.text: Will those leading duellists eschew fight with swords for judo?

definitions.note: judo is one example, hence the question mark

indicators.note: the leaders of a pair of words are their first letters

blocks.note: one's will is one's own self-direction, as in self-will
first letters of duellists and eschew
fencing is sword fighting as a sport

explanation.surface: A question whether duellists might drop swordplay and take up a martial art instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo is a Japanese martial art taught as a way of protecting yourself against an attacker.

clue.text: Excitement of the first whisky?

blocks.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky
A is the first, as in plan A versus plan B

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the thrill of their very first glass of Scotch.
explanation.walkthrough: The first whisky is labelled the way plans are, so the measure is followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama can mean exciting or emotional events, as in all the drama of the final.

clue.text: Delayed servant travels west, covering close to quarter of the Circle Line?

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means going right to left, backwards
the turned-round words cover, so enclose, the next letter
the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: late means delayed
a maid is a female servant
last letter of quarter

explanation.surface: A late-running maid heads west on London's Circle Line underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground line, but here it is a line across a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Diametral means relating to a diameter, the straight line through the centre of a circle.

clue.text: Set up cycling firm with capital taken from shark?

indicators.note: cycling rotates the word so its final letter comes round to the front
the capital is the first letter, and it is removed

blocks.note: stable means firm and steady
a shark is a fish, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A bicycle company is founded with money taken from a loan shark.
explanation.walkthrough: A shark is only one fish, which the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a business or institution is to found it and get it going.

clue.text: Unknown shot-stopper preserves goalless draw for manager of Wolves?

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe inside

blocks.note: Z is an algebraic unknown
a nil-nil scoreline looks like two zeros
a goalkeeper stops shots

explanation.surface: An obscure goalkeeper secures a 0-0 draw for the manager of Wolverhampton Wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, but the definition means real wolves in a zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A zookeeper looks after the animals at a zoo, so might be in charge of its wolf pack.

clue.text: Money made by secretary joining old boys in yacht on vacation

indicators.note: the secretary joins up with what follows, standing in front of it
the boys go inside the shell of the boat word
vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters remain

blocks.note: PA is a personal assistant
outer letters of yacht
boys who have grown old are men

explanation.surface: A secretary earns money by joining some old schoolfriends on a yachting holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment is a sum of money handed over, such as wages or a fee.

clue.text: Cut grass cut by rolling grass that’s come back up?

indicators.note: rolling over turns something round so it reads the other way
something cut by another is split open with the other inserted

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass
cud is food brought back up from a cow's stomach to be chewed again

explanation.surface: Mown grass is cut again by a roller, while cows chew the cud.
explanation.walkthrough: The first Cut is the definition; the second is the instruction to split the reed open.
explanation.definitionFit: Reduced means made smaller or lowered, as prices are when they are cut.

clue.text: Carried small child by the end of wearisome day

indicators.note: by means beside, so the next pieces come straight after
the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
last letter of wearisome
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A parent lugged a toddler around at the close of a tiring day.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or lug something, so toted is its past tense.

clue.text: Abolish naked attractions provided in New York

indicators.note: something naked is stripped, so the word loses its outer letters
the pieces sit inside the city abbreviation

blocks.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York
pulls are draws or attractions
if means provided that

explanation.definitionFit: To nullify a law or agreement is to cancel it and make it void.

clue.text: An hour after midnight, finally rub one’s feet

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: one in the morning, 1 am, with the Roman numeral for one
last letter of rub
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Late at night, at one in the morning, someone finally massages their own feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Feet here are units of verse rhythm, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of a short then a long syllable, and the Latin plural names several.

clue.text: Interrogate FBI agent lying about cheese boards

clue.text: Solomon’s accompanied by leaders in Galilee ordaining young gentiles

taken as written

clue.text: Presumably you’ve slept in this riverside hotel?
